title: Tier Sets
content: Tier sets are high-level armor sets obtained from raid bosses. Each tier provides significant stat bonuses when multiple pieces are equipped. Tier 1 (Molten Core), Tier 2 (Blackwing Lair), and Tier 3 (the original 40-player Naxxramas) are the Classic-era sets; the Burning Crusade and Wrath raids continued the numbering with Tier 4 through Tier 10. Tier sets are highly sought after for their power and prestige, and many players collect complete sets for achievements and bragging rights.

title: Legendary Weapons
content: Legendary weapons are the most powerful items in the game, requiring extensive quests and rare materials to obtain. Examples include Sulfuras, Hand of Ragnaros (assembled after defeating Ragnaros in Molten Core), Thunderfury, Blessed Blade of the Windseeker (pieced together through a Molten Core quest chain), and Atiesh, Greatstaff of the Guardian (a Naxxramas quest reward tied to the archmage Medivh's lore). These weapons have unique appearances, powerful stats, and often special abilities. Obtaining a legendary weapon is a major accomplishment that requires dedication and coordination with other players.

title: Profession Tools
content: Some professions need a tool carried in the bags before their recipes work at all: blacksmiths and engineers need a Blacksmith Hammer, enchanters a runed rod matched to their skill, miners a Mining Pick, and skinners a Skinning Knife. Crafting never fails in this game, so a tool is a requirement rather than a bonus to success. Other crafts need no tool of their own but do need the character standing beside the right stationary object, such as an anvil or a forge. Having good tools is essential for professional crafters who want to create high-quality items.

title: Mount Collection
content: World of Warcraft features hundreds of mounts with unique appearances and abilities. Rare mounts like the Ashes of Al'ar (Phoenix), Swift Zulian Tiger, or Deathcharger's Reins are highly prized. Some mounts are obtained through achievements, others through rare drops or expensive purchases. Mount collecting is a popular pastime. Epic flying mounts become available at level 70 with the appropriate riding skill.

title: Weapon and Armor Enchants
content: Enchants add magical properties to weapons and armor. Enchanters can create enchant scrolls or apply enchants directly. Popular weapon enchants include Crusader, Fiery Weapon, and Soulfrost, and any class can carry any of them. Armor enchants provide stats like +strength, +agility, or +spell power. Enchanting requires materials and skill. Good enchants can significantly improve gear performance.

title: Socketed Gems
content: Many high-level items have sockets that can hold gems to provide stat bonuses. Gem colors match socket colors for bonuses: red gems carry strength, agility, and spell power, yellow gems carry intellect and ratings like crit, hit, and haste, blue gems carry stamina, spirit, and mana per five seconds, and meta gems provide special effects. Jewelcrafters create gems from minerals. Gemming properly is crucial for optimizing character stats. Different specs require different gem priorities.

title: Consumable Items
content: Consumables are items that provide temporary benefits when used. Food provides stat buffs, potions restore health/mana or provide temporary boosts, elixirs give longer-lasting buffs, flasks provide raid buffs. Alchemists and cooks create many consumables. Using proper consumables before encounters is essential for raid and dungeon performance. Some consumables are very rare and expensive.

title: Trade Goods and Materials
content: Trade goods are materials used in professions. Cloth from humanoids, ore from mining nodes, leather from beasts, herbs from gathering. These materials are bought and sold on the auction house. Prices fluctuate based on demand. Professional players make gold by farming and selling materials. Understanding market values is important for both crafting and trading professions.

title: Dungeon and Raid Keys
content: Keys are special items that allow access to locked areas or higher difficulty content. Examples include The Master's Key (Karazhan), the Reservoir Key (heroic mode for the Coilfang Reservoir dungeons), the Auchenai Key (heroic mode for the Auchindoun dungeons), and the Medallion of Karabor (entry to the Black Temple). Some keys are obtained through quests, others from rare drops. Keys often require attunement processes. Having the right keys is necessary for accessing certain content.

title: Special Containers
content: Special containers hold unique items or provide access to rare rewards. Examples include the Cache of the Legion (a locked chest found in Tempest Keep: The Mechanar), the Bag of Fishing Treasures, or the Disgusting Oozeling (a companion pet found this way). Some containers are obtained from bosses, others from achievements or rare vendors. Opening containers provides excitement and potential valuable loot.

title: Guild and Faction Tabards
content: Tabards are cosmetic chest pieces that display guild or faction affiliation. Guild tabards show guild name and colors, faction tabards show allegiance to Horde/Alliance. Tabards are obtained through reputation grinds or purchases. Wearing tabards can affect gameplay in certain areas. Some tabards provide special abilities or are required for specific content.

title: PvP Equipment
content: PvP gear is specialized equipment for player vs player combat. Honor gear from battlegrounds, arena gear from rated matches. PvP sets provide resilience and PvP-specific stats. Weapons like the Grand Marshal's or High Warlord's sets are prestigious. PvP gear often has unique appearances. Players can mix PvP and PvE gear for hybrid builds.

title: Quest Reward Items
content: Many quests reward unique items that tell stories or provide character development. Examples include Quel'Serrar, forged at the end of a Dire Maul quest chain, and Thunderfury, finished by the quest Rise, Thunderfury! once its bindings drop in Molten Core. Quest rewards often have lore significance and unique appearances. Some quest items are essential for class stories. Collecting quest rewards helps players experience the game's narrative.

title: Cosmetic Items
content: There is no wardrobe or appearance-change system yet -- an item's look is simply whatever is equipped, so cosmetic collecting mostly means non-combat companion pets, which follow a player around and do nothing else. Pets are earned from vendors, quest rewards, holiday events, and rare drops, and many players collect them purely for their own sake. Some weapon enchants add a visual glow or proc animation as a side effect of their stat bonus, which is the closest thing to a customizable weapon appearance available this expansion. Holiday events also hand out costume items, like Hallow's End's wand that temporarily transforms the user into a ghost, ninja, pirate, skeleton, or leper gnome.

title: Relics and Artifacts
content: Relics are special items that provide bonuses to certain classes. Librams for paladins, idols for druids, totems for shamans. Relics go in the ranged weapon slot, where these classes would otherwise carry nothing, and provide unique bonuses. Some relics are very rare and powerful. Relics often have lore connections to class stories. Obtaining powerful relics is a goal for many players.
